big_story.headline: Shielding Agriculture, Expanding Trade
big_story.subhead: PIYUSH GOYAL ASSERTS NEW TRADE DEALS WILL PROTECT FARMERS WHILE BOOSTING EXPORTS
paragraphs: Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal has assured that upcoming trade agreements with major foreign partners will safeguard all sensitive domestic sectors. Addressing concerns over market opening, Goyal highlighted that the India-US trade deal will protect the interests of Indian farmers and critical industries. He emphasized that the deal is designed to give the country a strong comparative advantage on the global stage.

The trade push comes alongside a significant bilateral schedule with European partners as well. European leaders confirmed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to travel to Brussels in December to officially sign the India-EU trade deal. The agreement is expected to see a full rollout in mid-2027 as industries seek faster regulatory approvals and easier market access.

Despite prevailing global macroeconomic headwinds, the government remains optimistic about external trade metrics. Goyal stated that India can still achieve its ambitious target of $1 trillion in exports for the current fiscal year. Investors and trade groups will be closely monitoring how domestic policy protections align with foreign market concessions in the coming months.
big_story.pullbox: Safeguard measures in new trade pacts aim to protect Indian farmers while positioning domestic exporters to achieve the country's $1 trillion export target this fiscal year.

explains.title: What is Comparative Advantage?
paragraphs: Comparative advantage is an economic principle describing how a nation produces goods or services at a lower opportunity cost than its trading partners. Instead of trying to excel at everything, a country focuses resources on sectors where it holds the greatest relative efficiency.

In international trade negotiations, leveraging comparative advantage allows a nation to export its most competitive products while protecting sensitive domestic markets. This strategy helps boost overall trade volume without disrupting vulnerable local industries like agriculture.

Bengaluru-based artificial intelligence startup Simplismart has raised $14 million in its latest funding round. The investment round was led by Dallas VC along with participation from global tech leader NVIDIA, valuing the startup at $100 million.

The funding highlights growing investor appetite for foundational AI infrastructure technologies built out of India. Simplismart plans to utilize the newly raised capital to expand its engineering capabilities and scale its AI model deployment platform for global markets.

story_1.headline: Coal India Q2 Net Profit Jumps 53% to ₹6,516 Crore
paragraphs: Coal India reported a strong second-quarter performance, with net profit surging 53% year-on-year to ₹6,516 crore. Robust operational gains helped propel earnings growth despite recent global energy market volatility. Revenue expansion across major mining divisions supported the bottom-line performance.
In tandem with the profit growth, the board declared a second interim dividend for FY27. Shareholders are set to receive ₹10.25 per share, reinforcing the PSU's dividend yield profile.

story_2.headline: Brent Crude Nears $116 as Houthi Attacks Escalation
paragraphs: Global oil benchmarks spiked significantly as fresh Houthi drone strikes targeted key infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Brent crude advanced toward $116 per barrel as market participants priced in heightened geopolitical risks across the Middle East.
Traders caution that continued escalation could push prices higher toward $118 per barrel. The sharp rally presents fresh inflation challenges for energy-importing economies across Asia.

story_3.headline: Small Investors Dump Secondary Stocks for IPOs
paragraphs: India's retail investors are actively selling off secondary market holdings to fund participation in mainboard initial public offerings. Driven by substantial listing-day premiums, individual traders are reallocating capital into primary market issues. The strategic shift comes as secondary equity markets experience volatile rangebound trading.

geopolitics.headline: PM Modi to Travel to Brussels for India-EU Trade Pact
paragraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Brussels in December to officially sign the landmark India-EU Free Trade Agreement, as confirmed by the EU chief. The comprehensive trade deal is expected to roll out in mid-2027, marking a pivotal moment in bilateral economic relations. In preparation for the pact, Indian industry leaders are urging for faster regulatory approvals and easier market access across key sectors.

The agreement comes as Indian exporters aim to diversify trade channels and build long-term resilience against global economic headwinds. Business representatives emphasize that clear market access terms will be vital before the mid-2027 rollout takes effect. As final preparations ramp up for the December summit, domestic enterprises are aligning strategies to leverage enhanced trade pathways into European markets.

big_story.headline: Nitin Gadkari Highlights Infrastructure Path to $5 Trillion Economy
big_story.text: Speaking at the CII conference, Union Minister Nitin Gadkari emphasized that infrastructure plays a crucial role in building a $5 trillion Indian economy. He noted that expanding transit and logistics will help elevate India to the third-largest economy in the world. This focus guarantees sustained public spending across core infrastructure sectors.
